title: The Last Confession
premise: When the coffin of Harlan Voss, the town's revered founder, is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, concierge Jude Zhou becomes the only witness who can place a living man at the mausoleum on the night of the funeral—because Jude saw him, and stayed silent. As prosecutors prepare to charge Voss's widow with fraud, Jude is pulled between protecting their own buried past (a faked death they once helped stage) and exposing a conspiracy that reaches into the hotel's ownership. The investigation reveals Voss staged his own death to escape debts and reinvent himself, but his new identity was stolen from another missing man. In the end, Jude corners Voss in the hotel where it all began; rather than turn him in, Jude forces him to confess publicly before vanishing again themselves—choosing survival over justice, at last understanding its price.
about_author: Quentin Yarrow is the pen name of a former night-shift hotel worker who spent a decade watching strangers check in and out of other people's lives. They write mysteries about the invisible people who keep institutions running.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Brass
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Jude's POV. The exhumation draws a crowd to the cemetery; Jude watches from the service entrance as workers lift a coffin that weighs nothing at all. The town reels, and the widow Voss collapses. Jude recognizes something no one else does—a detail about the mausoleum door—and feels the old instinct to disappear war with a new, dangerous curiosity.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Signed the Book
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A detective named Okafor interviews hotel staff, and Jude realizes the guest register from the funeral weekend has been quietly removed. Flashbacks establish Jude's talent for noticing what guests want hidden. When Okafor mentions an unidentified man seen near the mausoleum, Jude lies smoothly—and hates how easily it comes.

chapters.title: The Founder's Suite
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Cleaning out the sealed Founder's Suite per management orders, Jude finds Harlan Voss's private ledger: payments to three names, one of which Jude recognizes from their own past. Meanwhile the district attorney announces fraud charges against the widow, and the town splits into believers and accusers. Jude pockets a single page.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Jude tracks the second name on the ledger to a drowned-man case from twenty years ago: Elias Marsh, declared dead upstream, body never found. Visiting Marsh's estranged sister, Jude hears about a brother who 'came back different' once. The chapter ends with Jude realizing Voss may have stolen not just money but a whole identity.

chapters.title: A Room Reserved Under No Name
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The detective works the case from the institutional side, pressured by city fathers to close it fast against the widow. Okafor notices the register page torn out and begins suspecting an insider. A quiet scene establishes Okafor's own history of looking away from powerful men, making her both threat and mirror to Jude.

chapters.title: The Trial Calendar
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. With the trial six weeks out, someone ransacks Jude's apartment—not stealing anything, just proving they could. Jude identifies the intruder's shoe print as hotel-issued. Management offers Jude a promotion clearly meant as a leash. Jude must decide whether to run, as they once did, or stand still for the first time.

chapters.title: Confession, Overheard
chapters.summary: Alternating close-third. Working a banquet, Jude overhears the hotel's owner—a Voss protégé—on the phone with a man whose voice matches recordings of the founder. Following the call's thread, Jude confirms Voss is alive, local, and being sheltered by the very institution that employs them. The stolen identity of Elias Marsh unravels further: Voss didn't just escape debt, he erased a living man.

chapters.title: Two Ghosts at One Window
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts the widow Voss privately and learns she has known for years—that her silence bought her children's futures. She begs Jude to let the lie stand. That night Jude finally tells Okafor everything except their own crime, trading partial truth for protection. The alliance is uneasy, transactional, real.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Climax. On the trial's eve, Voss himself checks into the hotel under the Marsh name, daring Jude to act. In the empty ballroom, the two survivors circle each other: Voss offers Jude partnership in invisibility; Jude counters with the ledger page and the sister's testimony. When the owner arrives to silence them both, a violent struggle ends with Okafor's arrival and Voss in handcuffs—but only because Jude chooses, finally, to be seen.

chapters.title: Checkout
chapters.summary: Resolution, Jude's POV. Voss confesses publicly; the widow's charges dissolve but her name never recovers, and she thanks Jude with cold eyes. Okafor quietly declines to pursue Jude's old crime—the price of survival acknowledged, not forgiven. Jude resigns from the hotel, leaving through the front door for the first time instead of the service entrance, and walks into an ordinary, visible morning.
